title: Mini salmon and potato cakes
summary: Soft little fish cakes made with just salmon and potato, no flour or salt. Easy to pick up and easy to batch-freeze.
texture: Soft, moist cakes that break apart easily. Serve whole for baby to hold and bite, or break into small soft pieces about the size of a pea for pincer-grasp practice.
ingredients: 1 medium potato (about 6 oz), peeled and cubed
1 tsp chopped fresh dill or a squeeze of lemon (optional)
1 tbsp olive oil, for the pan
steps: Boil the potato for 12 to 15 minutes until very soft. Drain and mash until smooth.
Meanwhile, steam or poach the salmon for 8 to 10 minutes, until it flakes easily and is opaque all the way through (145°F / 63°C).
Flake the salmon onto a plate and run your fingers through every piece to check for bones.
Mix the salmon into the potato with the dill, if using. Shape into about 10 small cakes, around 2 inches wide.
Warm the oil in a nonstick pan over medium-low heat and cook the cakes 3 minutes per side until lightly golden. Cool before serving.
choking: Fish bones are the biggest risk here: check every flake with your fingers, even in 'boneless' fillets.
Keep the cakes soft. If the outside crisps hard, break them open and offer the soft inside.

allergens.name: Fish
allergens.note: Fish is a common allergen. If salmon is new, offer a small taste of plain cooked salmon first. Salmon is one of the best fish choices for babies because it's low in mercury.

storage: Fridge up to 2 days. Freeze cooked, cooled cakes on a tray, then bag them, up to 1 month. Reheat until hot all the way through, then cool before serving.
tips: Use leftover cooked salmon from a family dinner, as long as it was cooked without salt or spicy seasoning.
Swap the potato for sweet potato for a sweeter, more colorful cake.
